<texte du visiteur>

Reference images, in order:
- The first image named "Uttu": a character from the cast: keep this exact character, same face, species, body, colours, outfit and logos. A picture with several views (a character sheet) still shows ONE character.
- The second image named "Quai": the place where the scene happens: the new picture is set in or on this place, never in a generic one. Keep its architecture, shapes, colours and materials; the characters are inside it at a believable scale. If the request names a part of it the pictures do not show (a deck, an interior, a street), build that part in the same design, colours and materials.
Use every image: each distinct character or creature appears once, whole and recognisable, with its own anatomy, colours and clothing; never merge two subjects into one. The images of a name define that name only: never lend its face, fur, colours, clothing or shapes to another name or to the place; the images of a place define only the setting. Poses, gestures and camera angle come from the request, never from the reference photos: give each character a fresh, natural pose that acts out the request. Compose ONE new finished picture, without reference panels, labels or contact-sheet layout.
Style: keep the rendering of the reference images; photographic references give a photographic picture, not a cartoon.
Staging for this picture, unless the request says otherwise: a wide shot, the characters small on the left third of the frame, the setting filling the rest. Pose every character for this staging and the action.
Style: keep the rendering of the reference images; photographic references give a photographic picture, not a cartoon.
